newsitem.title: UGANDA: U.N. Zaire envoy meets Uganda's Museveni.
newsitem.headline: U.N. Zaire envoy meets Uganda's Museveni.

text.p: A U.N. special envoy met Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni in Kampala on Sunday seeking crucial regional support for an international intervention force in eastern Zaire, officials at the presidency said.

They said Canadian diplomat Raymond Chretien, special envoy for the Great Lakes region, and Museveni discussed a role for Uganda -- possibly as a base for the international force to facilitate food distribution and other urgent needs of thousands of mainly Hutu refugees.

"The envoy has met President Museveni over a number of issues, key among them the international force and Uganda's role. Nothing more can be said at the moment," a senior official at the presidency told Reuters.
The officials said details were likely to emerge on Monday.
But senior political sources said Museveni appeared to be against France's presence in such a force, arguing that France was an interested party and would not be neutral.
That position has already been taken by Rwanda, whose president said last week that he backed an international humanitarian intervention force but French participation was not welcome.
On Sunday, Rwanda agreed to aid passing through its territory to the refugees but international relief workers were seeking a similar deal from rebels in the border area.
